'''Pernicar''' was the first [[Planet/Legends|planet]] orbiting the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Hoth's Brand]] in the [[Ruusan system/Legends|Ruusan system]] located in the [[Teraab sector/Legends|Teraab sector]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]. It was a scorching rock without any [[Moon/Legends|moons]]. Pernicar was named in honor of a [[Pernicar|Jedi Master]] who died during the [[Ruusan campaign]] at the end of the [[New Sith War]].

==History==
In [[2200 BBY/Legends|2200 BBY]],<ref name="EA" /> the [[Mining Guild/Legends|Mining Guild]] came to the [[Ruusan system/Legends|Ruusan system]] as part of a wave of expansion and [[Colonist/Legends|colonization]] that swept through the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim's]] newly established [[Teraab sector/Legends|Teraab sector]] and its young, [[Metal/Legends|metal]]-rich [[Star system/Legends|star systems]].<ref name="LD" /> However, the expected [[Mineral/Legends|mineral]] deposits proved disappointing, and by [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], the only remaining settlers were a handful of optimistic claim jumpers and those seeking refuge from creditors and [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]].<ref name="EA" />

[[File:Pernicar.jpg|right|thumb|240px|The planet was named in honor of the Jedi Master Pernicar]]
The system's location within a tangle of [[Nebula/Legends|nebulae]] and newborn [[Star/Legends|stars]] in the backwater of the sector seemingly doomed it to obscurity, had it not been for the fact that the third planet of the star system, [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]], became the site of epochal events. During the endgame of the [[Light and Darkness War]], Lord [[Hoth (Jedi Lord)|Hoth's]] [[Army of Light/Legends|Army of Light]] pursued the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] to Ruusan.<ref name="LD" /> Ultimately, both sides were [[Thought bomb|wiped out]], marking the end of the [[New Sith Wars]].<ref name="EA" /> To honor the memory of the participants in the pivotal [[Ruusan campaign]], the planets of the Ruusan system – renamed the Hoth's Brand system – were named after [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]].<ref name="Name">None of the sources have conclusively confirmed that the planets of the [[Ruusan system/Legends|Ruusan system]] were named after [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who participated in the [[Ruusan campaign]], with the exception of Pernicar and [[Othone]]. Nevertheless, the names of all the planets correspond to the names of Jedi. Therefore, the naming of the planets in the Ruusan system should be regarded as a tribute to the Jedi who participated in the campaign.</ref> In particular, the system's first planet was named in honor<ref name="CE" /> of the deceased [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Pernicar]].<ref name="JS">[[Jedi vs. Sith 4|''Jedi vs. Sith'' 4]]</ref>

Eventually, shifting nebulae within the stellar nursery of the Teraab sector erased the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace routes]] to Ruusan.<ref name="LD" /><ref name="EA" /> A few [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] after the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan|Battle of Ruusan]], the system had disappeared from most charts, remembered mainly by Jedi and Mining Guild archivists.<ref name="LD" />

==Behind the scenes==
All the planets of the [[Ruusan system/Legends|Ruusan system]] were introduced in the fifth installment of a set of scenarios, ''[[Kyle Katarn's Tale]]'', written by [[Abel G. Peña]] and [[Jason Fry]] for the [[Star Wars Miniatures]] game in [[2005]].<ref name="LD" /> Later, ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', a reference book co-authored by Jason Fry and [[Daniel Wallace]], placed the Ruusan star system in grid square P-11.<ref name="EA" />
